details.description: Llama 3 70B Instruct is Meta's 70-billion-parameter instruction-tuned model from the original Llama 3 family, released April 18, 2024, and optimized for assistant-like chat. Fireworks AI documents this specific "-hf" id as the original, full-precision (FP16) weights, matching the official Hugging Face release, as opposed to a quantized or otherwise modified variant. It is fine-tuned with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), uses Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), and has a knowledge cutoff of December 2023. This original Llama 3 has since been followed by Meta's longer-context Llama 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 and 4 releases.
advantages: Scores 82.0 on MMLU (5-shot), per Meta's model card.
Scores 81.7 pass@1 on HumanEval (0-shot), per Meta's model card.
Scores 93.0 on GSM-8K (8-shot, CoT), per Meta's model card.
Scores 50.4 on MATH (4-shot, CoT) and 39.5 on GPQA (0-shot), per Meta's model card.
Fireworks describes this id as the unmodified, full-precision (FP16) weights whose results should be consistent with Meta's official Hugging Face implementation, unlike a quantized deployment.
disadvantages: Meta's model card states Llama 3 is intended for commercial and research use in English only and was tested only in English.
Knowledge cutoff of December 2023, per Meta's model card.
Meta's model card does not describe tool-calling or function-calling support, unlike the later Llama 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3 releases.
Superseded by Meta's later Llama 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 and 4 releases, which extended the context window well beyond this model's 8K tokens, per those releases' model cards.
use_cases: Text extraction, classification, rewriting and summarization

notes: Same underlying Meta Llama 3 70B Instruct model as llama-v3-70b-instruct; Fireworks documents the '-hf' id specifically as the original FP16 weights matching the official Hugging Face release. Catalog's 8,192-token max_input/max_output matches Meta's model card (8k context) and Fireworks' hosted page (8.19k) for this model. The Llama 3 model card doesn't itself describe tool-calling or the later releases' longer context; confirmed on the Llama 3.1 model card (128k context, tool-use benchmarks). The use_cases list is confirmed on Meta's Llama 3 launch blog post, which lists advice, brainstorming, classification, question answering, coding, extraction, rewriting and summarization as evaluated use cases; not stated verbatim on the model card itself.
